nodes.statement: Let d_1(P) denote the number of pairs of points in P whose displacement w satisfies w \overline{w} = 1.

nodes.statement: Theorem 1 (Erdös construction): There exist point sets P of size n with d_1(P) \gg n^{1 + c/\log\log n}.
nodes.span: There exists point sets ${P}$ of arbitrarily large cardinality ${n}$ such that ${d_1(P) \gg n^{1 +c / \log\log n}}$
nodes.status_reason: Stated as a known theorem.

nodes.statement: Theorem 2 (OpenAI construction): There exist point sets P of size n with d_1(P) \gg n^{1 + c}.

nodes.statement: The constructions involve taking elements of a ring of algebraic integers up to a certain height.

nodes.statement: We use a product m of t primes of size T \asymp t \log t that are 1 mod 4.

nodes.statement: We take g distinct primes q_1, \dots, q_g of size G \asymp g \log g, with T > G.

nodes.statement: We work in the number field generated by i and the square roots of q_1, \dots, q_g.

nodes.statement: We use the naive ring of integers B generated by i and the square roots of q_i.

nodes.statement: The number of elements of B of height at most H is approximately H^D.

nodes.statement: B can be embedded as a lattice in C^{D/2}.
nodes.span: it is convenient to think of ${B}$ as a lattice in a ${D}$ -dimensional vector space

nodes.statement: The covolume of the lattice B is bounded by G^{O(gD)}.

nodes.statement: Any sublattice of B of index I contains a vector of height O(I^{1/D} G^{O(g)}).

nodes.statement: We seek a sublattice \Lambda of index m^{D/2} such that \Lambda \cdot \overline{\Lambda} \subset mB.
nodes.span: find some sublattice ${\Lambda}$ (in fact, they will be ideals, but we will not need this) of ${B}$ for which we can obtain the inclusion

nodes.statement: Such a sublattice \Lambda will contain a non-zero element w of height O(m^{1/2} G^{O(g)}), making w \overline{w} equal to m times an element of height O(G^{O(g)}).
nodes.span: ${\Lambda}$ will contain a non-zero element ${w}$ of height ${O(m^{1/2} G^{O(g)})}$
nodes.status_reason: Follows from Minkowski's theorem application and the inclusion property.

nodes.statement: There are at least 2^{tD/4} different sublattices \Lambda of index m^{D/2} that obey the inclusion condition.

nodes.status_reason: Follows from the prime-by-prime construction using the Chinese remainder theorem.

nodes.statement: For each prime p dividing m, there are 2^{D/4} sublattices \Lambda_p of index p^{D/2} obeying \Lambda_p \cdot \overline{\Lambda_p} \subset pB.
nodes.span: it suffices to show for each of the ${t}$ primes ${p}$ dividing ${m}$ , that there are ${2^{D/4}}$ different sublattices ${\Lambda_p}$
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the structure of B/pB.

nodes.statement: The ring B/pB can be embedded into a product of copies of F_p and F_{p^2}.
nodes.span: we can also embed ${B/pB}$ into a product of copies of ${{\mathbb F}_p}$ and ${{\mathbb F}_{p^2}}$
nodes.status_reason: Standard property of prime splitting in number fields.

nodes.statement: B/pB is isomorphic to F_p^D or F_{p^2}^{D/2}, organizing into conjugate pairs that generate at least 2^{D/4} subspaces V with V \cdot \overline{V} = 0.

nodes.status_reason: Follows from the embedding of B/pB and prime splitting.

nodes.statement: Minkowski's theorem generates 2^{tD/4} non-zero vectors w of height O(m^{1/2} G^{O(g)}) obeying the congruence equation.
